**STEP 1 - Scene:** This is a small side dish of sweet corn on the cob, cut into two cross-sections, on a white plate. The photo is taken from above at a steep, slightly tilted angle. The diced orange vegetables at the bottom-right are on a separate plate at the edge, so I'm excluding them.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The white plate is roughly 26 cm across at its longest undistorted width, so it is dinner-plate sized. Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Two cross-cut pieces of cooked corn on the cob (sweet corn). No visible butter, oil, or sauce.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The corn pieces cover about 15% of the plate (~80 cm²).

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Each piece is roughly a cylinder about 4.5 cm in diameter and 4 cm long, so about 64 ml each. Two pieces give ~130 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Whole cob pieces (kernels plus cob) use a bulk density of about 0.6 g/ml, giving ~78 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Boiled sweet corn is about 96 kcal per 100 g, so 78 g × 0.96 ≈ 75 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Two corn-cob pieces covering about 15% of a dinner plate should weigh roughly 70–90 g and about 70–90 kcal. The estimate fits.

Total: about 78 g, about 75 kcal.
